page_title: usage — Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Grok & Muse quota tracker

summary.name: usage
summary.one_liner: A macOS menu bar and Windows system tray app that shows AI coding-tool quota (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Grok, Muse Code) with reset times, tokens, and costs.
use_cases: Check remaining Claude Code or Codex quota before a big refactor
Track token spend and project costs across AI coding tools
Generate a shareable HTML usage report without project names
Monitor context size in Claude Code with status line warnings
Watch quota from a terminal on Linux with uvx
summary.what_it_does: The app shows how much of the 5-hour and 7-day quota has been used for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Grok and Muse Code, along with when each quota resets. On macOS the menu bar shows up to three tools with the highest session usage, and the panel lists all tools and project costs. It reads local files for Claude Code, Codex and Grok usage, and uses the sign-in of each vendor's own CLI for Antigravity and Muse. It can produce HTML reports for today, week, month or all-time with token and cost trends, top projects and model breakdowns. It also adds Claude Code helpers such as a context-percentage status line, Token Saver, Beginner Mode and Quota-Aware Mode.
notable: Menu bar and system tray quota display with reset countdowns for five AI coding tools
16 selectable panel themes and a compact layout for four or more quota cards
Local-first: reads local log files, and Muse quota uses a small model call through its signed-in CLI
Claude Code pane showing quotas, conversations and subagent status
caveats: Muse quota checks make a small model call that uses a little Muse quota
Beginner Mode uses a little Claude quota
macOS and Windows show security prompts on first launch that need manual approval
